newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RATE CUT IMMINENT ONCE CREDIT SLOWS -FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RATE CUT IMMINENT ONCE CREDIT SLOWS -FINMIN.

text.p: Polish official interest rates should be cut when a steady decline in inflation is accompanied by a lasting slow-down in credit growth, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
"If the slow-down (in credit) which we already see continues and inflation keeps falling, nominal rates should fall," Belka told Reuters in an interview.

Belka said that with year-on-year inflation at 17.3 percent in February and T-bill yields at 21.2 percent, real interest rates were already high and an expected further fall in inflation and the resulting real rate rise should eventually slow credit and trigger a rate cut some time this year.
"If we manage to shave further two points off current inflation in the next few months, real interest rates will rise to about six percent," Belka said.
"This would mean a radical change in interest policy given the fact that not so long ago real rates were close to zero," he added.

The central bank, which raised this month obligatory reserves on banking deposits to contain credit expansion, has said it needed to see a significant drop in credit growth before any rate move was considered.
Last year, lending to the non-financial sector rose 40 percent in nominal terms with consumer credit more then doubling.
Belka said he accepted the rise in real rates as the ministry shared the independent central bank's concern about the trade deficit, fuelled by booming domestic demand.
But the rise in real rates increased costs of public debt servicing. "We are accepting this (high real rates) with concern because it is increasing debt financing costs," Belka said.
